newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to keep public expenditure below 20 pct 97/98.
newsitem.headline: HK to keep public expenditure below 20 pct 97/98.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Thursday that it would keep total public spending at about 18.3 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997/98, the year the British colony reverts to China.
Secretary for the Treasury K.C. Kwong said GDP was estimated at HK$1,355,490 million for fiscal 1997 which starts on April 1.
Recurrent public spending is expected to grow by 5.3 percent in real terms within this overall growth recurrent government spending will grow by 5.6 percent
"This exceeds the growth guidelines of five percent as a consequence of underspending in 1996-97," the government said.
But in overall terms, the government stuck to its strict guidelines of keeping public spending growth within the bounds of GDP growth.
The British colony of Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997.
